sources.title: The Kra-Dai Languages
sources.note: Academic linguistic overview distinguishing Thai and Tai from the wider diverse Kra-Dai language family.

sources.title: Bronze Age wetland landscapes and political formations in southwest China
sources.note: Archaeological synthesis of Dian basin settlements, political economy, rice farming, livestock, bronze, and mortuary evidence.

sources.title: Pyu Ancient Cities World Heritage nomination dossier
sources.note: Official archaeological dossier for chronology, urban landscapes, water control, production, trade, religion, and burials.

sources.title: Kra-Dai Languages
sources.note: University linguistic overview of family diversity, modern distribution, and historical spread across southern China and Southeast Asia.

sources.title: Phylogenetic evidence reveals early Kra-Dai divergence and dispersal
sources.note: Peer-reviewed language-tree model whose uncertainty prevents assigning reconstructed speech to archaeological sites or broad polygons.

sources.title: Hunting and Rituals: Treasures from the Ancient Dian Kingdom
sources.note: Public museum account of excavated Dian cemeteries, bronzes, material culture, everyday scenes, warfare, and ritual.

sources.title: The Southwest Silk Road: artistic exchange and transmission in early China
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of Dian bronzes, cowrie containers, imagery, exchange, and distinctive lost-wax metalworking.

sources.title: Two-season agriculture and irrigated rice during the Dian
sources.note: Open research record for directly dated crops, mixed agriculture, vertical landscapes, seasonal cropping, and cautious irrigation inference.

sources.title: Gold Seal of the King of Dian
sources.note: National Museum of China object record for material, snake knob, seal-script inscription, find context, and 109 BCE interpretation.

sources.title: Seal of the King of Dian and Han relations
sources.note: Official contextual account connecting the excavated inscription with the 109 BCE settlement and its ambiguous political status.

sources.title: Dian cowrie container
sources.note: Official museum object page identifying a characteristic bronze cowrie container from the Dian cultural sphere.

sources.title: Dian cowrie container with weaving scene
sources.note: University library object record for a second-to-first-century BCE Shizhaishan bronze scene showing textile production.

sources.title: Cranial features of Dian Culture remains from Shaomaoshan cemetery
sources.note: Physical anthropology study demonstrating what skeletal analysis can investigate and the limits of one cemetery sample.

sources.title: Archaeological exploration of the Kele site
sources.note: Government report on Yelang-period tombs, relics, mapping, drones, soil survey, and continuing archaeological uncertainty.

sources.title: Yelang metallurgy and Han imperial governance of Southwest China
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of local and imported metal traditions and the shift toward Han commanderies after 135 BCE.

sources.title: Chemical datasets of ancient bronze drums from Guangxi
sources.note: Open scientific study of drum alloying, ore signatures, decoration, chronology, communication, and interpretive limits.

sources.title: Growth and Stability Among Complex Societies in Prehistoric Lingnan
sources.note: Archaeological regional study of rice communities, status differences, external contacts, and varied pathways before 200 BCE.

sources.title: From the Iron Age to early cities at Sri Ksetra and Beikthano
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis of early Pyu water control, iron, domestic ceramics, brickwork, funerary culture, literacy, and Buddhism.

sources.title: Pyu Ancient Cities conservation and archaeology report
sources.note: Official field report describing ritual buildings, wells, cremation deposits, and hundreds of burial urns at Sri Ksetra.

sources.title: Pyu Ancient Cities heritage workshop proceedings
sources.note: Institutional proceedings on excavation, conservation, mortuary remains, landscapes, and responsible interpretation of the Pyu sites.

sources.title: Mission Archéologique Française au Myanmar: past, present and future
sources.note: Project report on eleven seasons of collaborative late-prehistoric cemetery excavation in the Samon River valley.

sources.title: Infant and child burials in the Samon Valley, Myanmar
sources.note: Archaeological conference paper on child burial forms, grave grouping, miniature goods, and regional comparison.

sources.title: Excavation and physical anthropology at Ban Wang Hi
sources.note: Thai specialist database summarizing age groups, oral health, skeletal preservation, burial clusters, goods, and status interpretation.

sources.title: Excavation at Ban Wang Hi, Lamphun Province
sources.note: Detailed excavation report for a northern Thai cemetery used only as a just-outside-the-polygon edge comparator.

sources.title: King Ram Khamhaeng Inscription
sources.note: Thailand National Archives record dating the Thai-language Ram Khamhaeng inscription to 1292 CE.

sources.title: Records of the Grand Historian: Southwestern Yi
sources.note: Digitized primary text describing many southwestern leaders, settlements, farming, diplomacy, campaigns, and Han-era categories.

sources.title: Resettlement strategies and Han expansion into southwest China
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeological study of expansion from 135 BCE, migration, colonial encounters, Dian autonomy, and the 109 BCE seal.

sources.title: People and Plants in Ancient Southwest China
sources.note: Open scholarly synthesis of first-millennium BCE crops, Dian sites, environment, texts, exchange, and 122 to 109 BCE events.

sources.title: China’s Early Impact on Eastern Yunnan
sources.note: Archaeological comparison of historical accounts with Dian burial objects before and after Han incorporation.

sources.title: Rediscovering the settlement system of the Dian kingdom
sources.note: Peer-reviewed landscape survey mapping Dian settlements, hierarchy, wetlands, political centers, and later imperial reorganization.

sources.title: Reconsidering social hierarchy in Dian culture
sources.note: Mortuary analysis of hundreds of Dian graves testing hierarchy while warning against conflating texts, images, and burials.

sources.title: Preliminary findings from the Lake Dian Basin survey
sources.note: Joint archaeological survey report covering fieldwalking, cores, Bronze Age sites, and mixed Bronze Age to Han remains.

sources.title: A First-Century Stele from Sriksetra
sources.note: Scholarly chronology review reporting broad radiocarbon ranges and the need to separate earliest activity from later cities.

sources.title: Water Management System of Sriksetra and Beikthano
sources.note: Research presentation on canals, reservoirs, drainage, water capture, and interpretation at two Pyu cities.

sources.title: New evidence for Sri Ksetra water management
sources.note: Archaeology conference abstract emphasizing phased water systems, radiocarbon evidence, and later landscape alteration.

proposedOverrides.summary: A cautious guide to the many Dian, Pyu, Himalayan, and other communities hidden beneath an anachronistic 200 to 100 BCE “Thai” atlas label.
